365666.title: Harary's edge reconstruction conjecture
365666.literal_statement:
Let $G=(V,E)$) be a finite simple graph with $|E|>4$. For each edge of $G$, let $G_i$ denote the maximal subgraph obtained by deleting that edge, and define the **edge deck** of $G$ by

$$
\operatorname{Deck}(G)\coloneqq\{G_i\}_{i=1}^m.
$$

**Harary's reconstruction conjecture.** If $\operatorname{Deck}(G)=\operatorname{Deck}(H)$ for some graph $H$, then $G\cong H$.

This conjecture asserts that every graph with more than four edges is uniquely determined, up to isomorphism, by its maximal edge-deleted subgraphs. The paper proves it for graphs with exactly one cycle and three non-isomorphic subtrees; the general conjecture remains open.
365666.ordinary_attempt_and_precise_gap: Need injectivity of the edge-deck map on every finite simple graph with >4 edges. Single-cycle/three-subtree results do not cover arbitrary graphs. Generalized multiset collision at 361991 gives no pair of individual equal decks.
365666.actual_review_depth: Source introduction, exact conjecture and restricted unicyclic statement; no full general proof

365866.title: Thomassen's conjecture on balanced clique subdivisions

This is posed as a strengthening related to Mader's conjecture; the supplied text does not state whether it has been resolved.

357190.title: The polynomial-time recognition conjecture for reduced clique graphs of chordal graphs
357190.literal_statement:
For a graph $G$, let $C_R(G)$ denote its reduced clique graph. A graph is **chordal** if it has no induced cycle of length at least four. The recognition problem asks whether a given graph is isomorphic to $C_R(G)$ for some chordal graph $G$.

**Reduced clique graph recognition conjecture.** There is a polynomial-time algorithm for deciding whether a given graph is isomorphic to $C_R(G)$ for some chordal graph $G$.

Polynomial-time recognition is known for clique graphs of chordal graphs, but the source says that the corresponding techniques do not obviously extend to reduced clique graphs. The conjectured algorithm is therefore presented as an open problem.

A clique-tree characterization for a supplied chordal graph does not recognize which arbitrary graphs arise as reduced clique graphs. 359851.title: The fixed--modular integer programming tractability conjecture
359851.literal_statement:
Let $\Delta \in \mathbb{Z}_{>0}$ be fixed. An integer program of the form (IP) has a constraint matrix $B$ that is **$\Delta$-modular** if its full-rank minors have absolute value at most $\Delta$ and at least one has absolute value $\Delta$.

**Fixed-$\Delta$ tractability conjecture.** There is a polynomial-time algorithm to solve any integer program of the form (IP) with a $\Delta$-modular constraint matrix.

This conjecture extends the polynomial-time solvability of totally unimodular integer programs to every fixed bound on the maximal non-vanishing subdeterminants. Its status is not resolved in the supplied text.
359851.ordinary_attempt_and_precise_gap: Rank is unbounded. Fixed dimension algorithms or generic-matrix bounds do not produce polynomial running time at fixed determinant bound. Need an algorithm polynomial in total binary encoding length for all ranks and all feasible/infeasible/unbounded instances; source Conjecture 1.1 remains beyond read special cases.

374654.title: Geelen's coarse Gallai conjecture for A-paths
374654.literal_statement: Let $G$ be a finite or infinite graph and let $A\subseteq V(G)$. An **$A$-path** is a path in $G$ between two distinct vertices of $A$. Two subgraphs are at distance at least $r$ when the distance between their vertex sets is at least $r$. A set is **$(a,b)$-centered** if it is contained in the union of at most $a$ balls of radius at most $b$. **Geelen's coarse Gallai conjecture.** There exist functions $f,g:\mathbb N\rightarrow\mathbb R$ such that for any $k,r\in\mathbb N$, graph $G$ and $A\subseteq V(G)$, either there exist $k$ $A$-paths pairwise at distance in $G$ at least $r$, or there exists a set $(f(k),g(r))$-centered in $G$ intersecting all $A$-paths. The conjecture is a coarse version of Gallai's packing-covering theorem for $A$-paths. The source does not state a resolution; its exact original formulation was reported as lost, and this is the formulation attributed to Geelen by Hendrey and Jacobs.
374654.ordinary_attempt_and_precise_gap: Need packing at distance r or hitting by f(k) balls of radius g(r), with neither bound acquiring the other parameter. Source Conjecture 1.5 and known bound (4k-4,256^k r) do not close this. Coarse Menger refutations in metadata are not automatically A-path refutations.

359186.title: The radial tree-width conjecture for graphs excluding quasi-geodesic subdivisions of the triangle
359186.literal_statement:
Let $G$ be a connected graph. For $c,k\in\mathbb{N}$, a **$c$-quasi-geodesic $(\geqslant ck)$-subdivision of $K^3$** means a subdivision of the triangle whose subdivided paths are $c$-quasi-geodesic and have length at least $ck$. The **radial tree-width** of $G$ is the tree-width notion defined for radial decompositions.

**Radial tree-width conjecture.** There is a function $f:\mathbb{N}\rightarrow\mathbb{N}$ such that, if a connected graph $G$ does not contain a $c$-quasi-geodesic $(\geqslant ck)$-subdivision of $K^3$ for some $c,k\in\mathbb{N}$, then

$$
\operatorname{radial\ tree\text{-}width}(G)\leqslant f(k).
$$

The preceding discussion explains that the subdivided-star argument does not directly produce a quasi-geodesic structural subgraph and presents this assertion as an unresolved question for trees. No resolution is given in the supplied text.

Need precise equivalence to literal three-path quasi-geodesic subdivision and parameter conventions. Appendix B shows the natural subgraph/decomposition technique fails. 360166.title: Langhede and Thomassen's exponential correspondence-colouring conjecture for planar graphs
360166.literal_statement:
Let $G$ be a planar graph. A **correspondence assignment** $(L,M)$ for $G$ consists of a list assignment $L$ and, for each edge, a partial matching between the corresponding vertex-colour pairs; an $(L,M)$-colouring chooses a colour from each list while avoiding matched pairs on every edge. The class of planar graphs has exponentially many $5$-correspondence colourings if there exists a constant $c>0$ such that every planar graph $G$ and every $5$-correspondence assignment $(L,M)$ admit at least $2^{c\cdot v(G)}$ distinct $(L,M)$-colourings.

**Langhede and Thomassen's conjecture.** Planar graphs have exponentially many $5$-correspondence colourings.

This conjecture asks for an exponential strengthening of the known $5$-correspondence-colourability of planar graphs. The source gives no resolution, so the conjecture remains open.
360166.ordinary_attempt_and_precise_gap: Theorem 1.5 gives 2^(v/67) colourings for arbitrary 5-correspondence assignment. Choose c=1/67. Actual proof using Theorem 3.2 read; source theorem already exactly resolves endpoint. Journal repository read, full journal PDF new 403 respected.

358526.title: Scott and Seymour's tournament-local chromatic number conjecture
358526.literal_statement:
Let $G$ be a graph and $T$ a tournament on the same vertex set. For a vertex $v$, write $N_T^+(v)$ for its out-neighbourhood in $T$.

**Scott and Seymour's conjecture.** For every positive integer $k$ there exists a positive integer $\chi$ such that, for every graph $G$ with $\chi(G) \geqslant \chi$ and every tournament $T$ on the same vertex set, there is a vertex $v$ such that

$$
\chi(G[N_T^+(v)])\geqslant k.
$$

The paper disproves this conjecture, so the proposed implication does not hold in general.

375388.title: Georgakopoulos–Papasoglu fat minor conjecture
375388.literal_statement:
Let $X$ and $G$ be graphs, let $K\in\mathbb{N}$, and let $f:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}^2$ be a function. A graph is **$K$-fat-minor-free with respect to $X$** when it does not contain $X$ as a $K$-fat minor.

**Fat minor conjecture.** For every graph $X$ there exists a function $f:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}^2$ such that, for every graph $G$ and $K\in\mathbb{N}$, if $G$ does not contain $X$ as a $K$-fat minor, then $G$ is $f(K)$-quasi-isometric to a graph with no $X$ minor.

This conjecture has been disproved, with further counterexamples showing failure even for certain small graphs and under a weakened conclusion. It is therefore refuted rather than open.
375388.ordinary_attempt_and_precise_gap: Source Conjecture 5.2 exactly matches, then reports public refutations and stronger later counterexamples. Original Davies et al. and later counterexample proofs not acquired/read here, so independently reconstructing a model and quasi-isometry obstruction remains unpaid. 367643.title: Ulam–Kelly reconstruction conjecture for graph homomorphism counts
367643.literal_statement: Let $Hom(F,G)$ denote the number of graph homomorphisms from $F$ to $G$, and let $\mathcal{G}$ be the family of all graphs. For a family of graphs $\mathcal{F}$, say that $Hom(\mathcal{F},\cdot)$ is reconstructible if, for every graph $G$ with at least three vertices, the vector of homomorphism counts $Hom(\mathcal{F},G)$ is uniquely determined by the vectors $Hom(\mathcal{F},G\setminus i)$ for every vertex $i$ of $G$. **Ulam–Kelly reconstruction conjecture.** $Hom(\mathcal{G},\cdot)$ is reconstructible. This is the homomorphism-count formulation of the Ulam–Kelly graph reconstruction conjecture, asserting that a graph with at least three vertices is determined up to isomorphism by the collection of its vertex-deleted subgraphs. The source presents this formulation as a motivation and question; no resolution is given here.

374380.title: Hardness conjecture for bounded-size inversion approximation
374380.literal_statement:
Let $p\geq 3$ and $k\geq 1$ be integers. For a digraph $D$, let $\operatorname{sinv}_{k}^{\leq p}(D)$ denote the optimization problem of making $D$ $k$-arc-strong using inversions of size at most $p$.

**Bounded-size inversion approximation hardness conjecture.** There exists $\varepsilon>0$ such that, unless $P=NP$, for every $p\geq 3$ and every $k\geq 1$, no polynomial-time $(1+\varepsilon)$-approximation algorithm for $\operatorname{sinv}_{k}^{\leq p}$ in digraphs exists.

The conjecture asserts that increasing the allowed inversion size does not make the approximation problem easier. It is presented as an open conjecture in the source.

367858.title: Generalized Erdős–Rogers polynomial-growth conjecture for hypergraphs
367858.literal_statement:
Let $F$ and $G$ be $r$-graphs, meaning $r$-uniform hypergraphs, and let $f_{F,G}(n)$ denote the generalized Erdős–Rogers number. An **$F$-iterated blowup** is the hypergraph obtained by repeatedly applying the blowup construction determined by $F$.

**Generalized Erdős–Rogers polynomial-growth conjecture.** There exists a constant $c=c(F,G)$ such that

$$
f_{F,G}(n)\ge n^c
$$

if and only if $G$ is a subgraph of an $F$-iterated blowup.

This extends the cited conjecture for $F=K^3_3$ to arbitrary $r$-graphs $F$ and $G$. The source proposes it as an extension, and no resolution is given.

369168.title: Nash-Williams' Chvátal-type conjecture for Hamilton cycles in digraphs
369168.literal_statement:
Let $G$ be a strongly connected digraph on $n\geq 3$ vertices, and let $d^+_1\leq\cdots\leq d^+_n$ and $d^-_1\leq\cdots\leq d^-_n$ be its ordered outdegree and indegree sequences. **Nash-Williams' conjecture.** If, for every $i<n/2$, 

$$
d^+_i\geq i+1\text{ or }d^-_{n-i}\geq n-i,
$$

and

$$
d^-_i\geq i+1\text{ or }d^+_{n-i}\geq n-i,
$$

then $G$ contains a Hamilton cycle. This is a directed analogue of Chvátal's best-possible degree-sequence condition; its status is not resolved in the supplied source.

361991.title: The generalized edge reconstruction conjecture
361991.literal_statement: Let $n\geq 4$, and let $G_1,\dots,G_k$ be a collection of $n$-edged graphs for some $k\geq 1$. Write $\coprod_{i=1}^k\operatorname{ED}(G_i)$ for the disjoint union of their edge decks. **Generalized edge reconstruction conjecture.** For every $k\geq 1$, the collection $\{G_1,\dots,G_k\}$ is uniquely reconstructible from $\coprod_{i=1}^k\operatorname{ED}(G_i)$. This is explicitly disproved in the paper: for every $n\geq 2$, some finite collection is not reconstructible, so the conjecture is false.
361991.ordinary_attempt_and_precise_gap: Complete n=4,k=4,five-vertex multiset witness written and all edge deletions classified by hand. Source v1/v2 and actual journal Theorems 3.20-3.22 already refute full endpoint; source kernel derivation even gives k4<=2. Explicit witness is a subsumed helper/variant, no credit.

362427.title: Grzesik–Lee–Lidický–Volec conjecture on apices of Sidorenko graphs
362427.literal_statement: Let $G$ be a connected graph with the Sidorenko property. For an integer $k$, the **$k$-apex** of $G$ is obtained by adding $k$ independent vertices, each adjacent to every vertex of $G$. **Grzesik–Lee–Lidický–Volec conjecture.** The $k$-apex of $G$ is common for every $k$. This conjecture concerns the classification of common graphs, where a graph is common when its Ramsey multiplicity equals the random-coloring benchmark. The paper proves the assertion for $k\leq 5$ when $G$ is a tree, while the general conjecture remains open.
362427.ordinary_attempt_and_precise_gap: Need all connected Sidorenko graphs and arbitrary nonnegative k. Source tree k<=5 results do not cover arbitrary Sidorenko bases or arbitrary apex count; no inequality closes both gaps. Sidorenko property of base does not automatically imply the required monochromatic cone inequality.
